messages:
maria.ops: FYI - Customer Acme reported a spike of 504s and 5xxs from hosted API around 15:30 UTC. They see long tail timeouts, repro attached: request ids: r-9a3f,r-9a41. They say requests briefly succeed then later fail with timeouts.

jonathan.dev: Looking at ingestion graphs for the cluster - request_queue_depth jumped to ~95% at 15:28 and stayed high for ~4m. Continuous-batching backlog increased, lots of long-lived KV cache warmups.

maria.ops: Customer trace (redacted) shows backend gateway 504. Snippet: ```
2026-03-15T15:28:37Z host gateway: request_id=r-9a3f status=504 reason=\"queue_timeout\" queue_depth=189 route=/v1/generate tenant=acme
```

jonathan.dev: I ran a quick query on metrics: `sum(rate(requests_total{route=\"/v1/generate\"}[1m])) by (tenant)` + `queue_depth` series — pattern looks like a tight burst from a single tenant then degraded batching throughput. Looks like queue depth limit + continuous batching not collapsing properly when many long-seqs hit.

sre-bot: ALERT: hosted-gateway.request_queue_depth > 85% for 3m (cluster: hosted-prod-7). See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/queue-saturation (auto-notify).

kevin.se: Repro steps I used (lightweight):
```bash
# 100 parallel clients, each sends a longseq prompt to force kv-cache build
for i in {1..100}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ \
    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \ \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ \
    -d '{\"model\":\"open-llm-large\",\"input\":\"<long prompt>...\",\"max_tokens\":512}' &\ndone\nwait\n```
This reliably produces queue_depth spikes on my dev cluster. Suggest trying tenant-scoped replay to match customer traffic shape.

sam.support: Customer says billing shows many partial attempts (error responses) which is frustrating. They want a temp fix while we triage. Customer timezone = PST, high priority.

jonathan.dev: Short-term mitigation options: 1) apply tenant throttle (rate-limit) to dial down concurrency, 2) pin tenant to smaller model variant with shorter KV warmups, 3) increase route queue_limit for the tenant (risky). I'd try (1) + (2) first.

maria.ops: Kevin, can you run a controlled throttle for Acme and test with their replay? If it reduces 504s we can offer as mitigation. Also capture diagnostics: stacking histograms p50/p95/p99 and batching sizes.

kevin.se: Implemented tenant throttle (rate-limited to 0.6x observed peak) for tenant=acme at 15:46 UTC. Within ~90s we saw queue_depth drop to ~40% and gateway 504 rate cut by ~80%. I pushed traces: `trace://hosted-prod-7/trace/r-9a3f` (internal).

jonathan.dev: Root cause hypothesis: a short-lived tenant burst of long-sequence requests causes continuous-batcher to accumulate many inflight KV initialization steps. Since queue depth limit was close to default and batching didn't preempt older requests, tail-latency grows -> timeouts. Need two fixes: improve preemption/backpressure in the batcher and add a tenant-aware queue headroom policy.

maria.ops: Agreed. Action items: 
- kevin.se: keep throttle in place until we coordinate with customer (owner).
- jonathan.dev: draft a small change to batcher preemption (disable waiting for full batch if oldest-request-age > 150ms) and test on canary.
- sam.support: propose mitigation options to customer and offer temporary throttle + credits for failed attempts.

sam.support: I've messaged Acme with the temporary throttle plan and offered a credit. They accepted a 1-hour throttle window while we test changes.

jonathan.dev: I'll open a PR for the batcher preemption experiment and schedule a canary rollout tomorrow to 10% of traffic. PR: https://git.redwood/pr/7482.

maria.ops: Great. Marking incident as \"investigating -> mitigated customer-facing\" for now. Will reopen if we see another spike. :thumbsup:
__note: This file conforms to slack/agents.md: messages field is a single continuous string of chronological Slack messages. All JSON values are strings or list of strings.
